div.head: Ger 11

ab.seg: [11[a]] on wintra erian ⁊ in miclum gefyrstum timber cleofan,
[11[b]] orceard ræran ⁊ mænige inweorc wyrcean, ðerhsan, wudu cleofan, hryðeran styllan, swyn stigian,
[11[c]] on odene cylne macian —
[11[d]] ofn ⁊ aste ⁊ fela ðinga sceal to tune — ge eac henna hrost;
On wintra erian 7 in miclum gefyrstum . tim|ber cleofan.
On wintra erian and in miclum gefyrstum timber cleofan,
orceard ræran and mænige inweorc wyrcean, ðerhsan, wudu cleofan, hryðeran styllan, swyn stician,
on odene cylne macian,
ofn and aste and fela ðinga sceal to tune, ge eac henna hrost.
im Winter pflügen und in grossen Frösten Bauholz spalten,
Garten bauen und viele Arbeiten innerhalb [des Gehöfts] thun, dreschen, Holz spalten, den Rindern Stall machen, Schweine einpferchen,
auf dem Dreschplatz eine Darre machen —
Ofen und Trockenofen und viele Dinge gehören zum Gutsgehöft — wie auch Hühnersteige;
in winter plough, and in hard frosts split timber,
lay out an orchard and do many indoor tasks, thresh, split wood, make stalls for the cattle, pen the pigs,
make a kiln on the threshing-floor —
an oven and a drying-kiln and many things belong to the estate — and also a hen-roost;
During the winter to plough and during the great frost to cleave timber.
To tend the orchard and to undertake many indoor duties, threshing, to cleave wood, put cattle in stalls, slaughter pigs.
To make a kiln on the threshing-floor.
[To make] an oven and a kiln, and many things must [be done] about the estate, likewise [to make] chicken roosts.
During the winter, one is to plow, fell trees during the great frost,
tend to the orchard, carry out indoor tasks, thresh, chop wood, put cattle in stalls, put pigs in their sty,
construct a kiln on the threshing floor and an oven and an oast,
and do many other things on the estate such as building chicken roosts.
Orceard ræran . 7 mænige inweorc wyrcean. ðerhsan . wudu cleofan . hryðeran styllan. swyn stygian .
On odene cylne macian .
Ofn . 7 aste . 7 fela ðinga sceal|to tune ge eac henna hrost .

note.seg: Jede Hufe zu Stoke liefert dem Herrn 4 foðera aclofenas gavolwyda; Bi 594. Das wudu nächster Z. ist also Brennholz
Each hide at Stoke supplies the lord with 4 foðera aclofenas gavolwyda; Bi 594. The wudu of the next l. is therefore firewood
Vgl. Gl Garten; dazu Hoops in Reallex. Germ. Altt. 113
Cf. Gl Garten; also Hoops in Reallex. Germ. Altt. 113

div.note: a kiln on the threshing floor and an oven and an oast: The kiln and the oven were used to dry the harvest for preservation. An oast was a kiln specially designed for drying hops.

note.seg: Nicht gemäss heutigem kiln ‘Ziegelei’, die gewiss nicht auf dem Domänenplatz lag; ‘Ofen’ Sweet, Kluge, ‘Feuerherd’ Sk-Wi zu weit; Ælfric glossiert siccatorium; bei Mätzner ustrina, torral (s. Ducange s. v.), also für Korn und Malz.—Zu folg. Z. ofn ‘Backofen’ Sk-Wi; zu ast: provinziell lebt noch oast ‘Gerstendarre zur Malzbereitung’; Wright Dial. dict.; ‘Dörrofen’ Sk-Wi

Not in the sense of present-day kiln ‘brickworks’, which certainly did not stand in the demesne yard; ‘oven’ Sweet, Kluge, ‘hearth’ Sk-Wi too wide; Ælfric glosses siccatorium; in Mätzner ustrina, torral (see Ducange s. v.), thus for grain and malt.—On the following l.: ofn ‘bake-oven’ Sk-Wi; on ast: oast ‘barley-kiln for malting’ still survives in provincial use; Wright Dial. dict.; ‘drying-oven’ Sk-Wi
